quick: RA/PsA: 5 mg PO BID or 11 mg XR once daily
With or without food; XR tablet swallowed whole
Avoid breastfeeding during and 18 h (IR)/36 h (XR) after
Reduce dose in moderate; avoid in severe
Lymphocytes, neutrophils, Hb, LFTs, lipids, TB, infection signs
summary: Tofacitinib is an oral JAK inhibitor for rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, ulcerative colitis and polyarticular JIA. Typical dose is 5 mg twice daily (immediate-release) or 11 mg once daily (extended-release). It carries a boxed warning for serious infections, mortality, malignancy, major adverse cardiovascular events and thrombosis.
indications: Moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis with inadequate response/intolerance to one or more TNF blockers
Active psoriatic arthritis with inadequate response/intolerance to one or more TNF blockers
Active ankylosing spondylitis with inadequate response/intolerance to one or more TNF blockers
Moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis with inadequate response/intolerance to TNF blockers
Active polyarticular course juvenile idiopathic arthritis (oral solution/tablets) in patients >=2 years

dosage.d: 5 mg IR twice daily or 11 mg XR once daily
dosage.n: Lowest effective dose; not with biologic DMARDs/potent immunosuppressants

dosage.d: 10 mg twice daily for at least 8 weeks
dosage.n: Up to 16 weeks; discontinue if no benefit

dosage.d: 5 mg twice daily (10 mg BID only if needed, limited duration)
Weight-based: 3.2 mg BID solution (10-20 kg) up to 5 mg BID (>=40 kg)
dosage.n: Use oral solution for small children

dosage.c: Renal/hepatic impairment or strong CYP inhibitors
dosage.d: Reduce to half the total daily dose

admin: Before starting, evaluate for active and latent TB, screen for viral hepatitis, obtain CBC, and update immunizations
Do not initiate if absolute lymphocyte count <500, ANC <1000, or hemoglobin <9 g/dL
Swallow extended-release tablets whole; do not crush, split or chew
May be taken with or without food
Extended-release (11 mg XR) and immediate-release (5 mg) are not interchangeable on a per-tablet basis
moa: Tofacitinib inhibits Janus kinases (predominantly JAK1 and JAK3, with lesser JAK2 activity), interrupting the JAK-STAT signaling pathway. This blocks signaling of multiple cytokines and growth factors involved in inflammation and immune cell function, reducing inflammatory and immune responses.

relative: Active serious infection including localized infection or TB
Lymphocyte count <500, ANC <1000 or Hb <9 g/dL
Concurrent biologic DMARDs or potent immunosuppressants
monitor: Cardiovascular risk factors / current or past smokers (MACE, malignancy risk)
Latent or chronic infections (hepatitis, herpes zoster)

preg: Avoid during pregnancy; based on animal data it may cause fetal harm. Advise effective contraception during treatment. A pregnancy exposure registry exists.
lact: Avoid breastfeeding during treatment and for 18 hours after the last immediate-release dose or 36 hours after the last extended-release dose due to potential serious adverse effects in the infant.
renal: No adjustment in mild renal impairment. In moderate to severe renal impairment (including those on hemodialysis), reduce the total daily dose by half (e.g., 5 mg once daily for RA).
hepatic: No adjustment in mild hepatic impairment. In moderate hepatic impairment, reduce the total daily dose by half. Use is not recommended in severe hepatic impairment.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole) - reduce tofacitinib dose
Biologic DMARDs / potent immunosuppressants (azathioprine, cyclosporine) - increased immunosuppression, not recommended
moderate: Moderate CYP3A4 plus potent CYP2C19 inhibitors (e.g., fluconazole) - reduce dose
Strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin) - reduced efficacy, avoid
minor: Methotrexate - no clinically significant PK interaction but increased immunosuppression
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; high-fat meal does not meaningfully alter exposure.
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol; potential additive hepatic effects and infection risk.
interactions.diagnostics: Can lower lymphocytes/neutrophils/hemoglobin, raise LDL/HDL cholesterol and elevate liver enzymes and creatine kinase.

serious: Serious and opportunistic infections (including TB, herpes zoster)

monitoring: Lymphocyte count, neutrophil count and hemoglobin at baseline, after 4-8 weeks and periodically
Latent/active TB before and during therapy; viral hepatitis screening
Signs of infection, thrombosis, cardiovascular events and malignancy
counsel: Report fever, cough, burning urination, painful skin rash (shingles) or other signs of infection promptly
Seek emergency care for chest pain, shortness of breath, leg swelling/pain or sudden weakness
Avoid live vaccines; keep immunizations up to date before starting
Tell your doctor if you smoke or have had cancer, clots or heart disease
Do not crush or split the extended-release tablet
pearls: BOXED WARNING: serious infections, mortality, malignancy, major adverse cardiovascular events and thrombosis
Higher risk of MACE, malignancy and death seen versus TNF blockers in RA patients >=50 yr with a CV risk factor - reserve for inadequate TNF response
Screen and treat latent TB and viral hepatitis before initiating
Do not combine with biologic DMARDs or potent immunosuppressants
Halve the dose with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and in moderate-severe renal or moderate hepatic impairment
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; in that case skip it and resume the schedule. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: There is no specific antidote. Pharmacokinetic data suggest more than 95% of a dose is eliminated within 24 hours. Treat overdose with supportive care and monitor for adverse reactions.
